# FIT5145 Assignment 1 & 3: Data-Driven Pacing Corridor for HYROX Athletes

## Dataset Source

In this demonstration, the datasets are obtained by websracping and saved into csv files named:

- hyrox_season8_male_pro.csv
- hyrox_season8_female_pro.csv

These datasets has been published to excelyynxl-a11 GitHub repository (link: <https://github.com/excelyynxl-a11y/fit5145/tree/main/ass1_3>). You can download the csv files and saved them into a data folder to carry out this demonstration.

## Load library

```{R}
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(hms)
library(randomForest)
library(caret)
```

## Load dataset

Season 8 Male Pro dataset.

```{R}
szn8_male_pro <- read_csv("data/hyrox_season8_male_pro.csv")
glimpse(szn8_male_pro)
```

Season 8 Female Pro dataset.

```{R}
szn8_female_pro <- read_csv("data/hyrox_season8_female_pro.csv")
glimpse(szn8_female_pro)
```

## Data cleaning

### Inspect szn8_male_pro

Convert all time split into \<time\> format

```{R}
# Define all split columns
run_cols <- paste0("Running_", 1:8)
station_cols <- c(
  "SkiErg_1000m", 
  "Sled_Push_50m", 
  "Sled_Pull_50m",
  "Burpee_Broad_Jump_80m", 
  "Row_1000m", 
  "Farmers_Carry_200m",
  "Sandbag_Lunges_100m", 
  "Wall_Balls"
)
all_time_cols <- c("Total_Time", "Roxzone_Time", run_cols, station_cols)

```

```{R}
# Standardize all time columns to strict <time> (hms class)
time_fomatted_male <- szn8_male_pro %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      all_of(all_time_cols),
      ~ if (inherits(.x, "hms") || inherits(.x, "difftime")) {
          hms::as_hms(as.numeric(.x))
        } else {
          hms::as_hms(period_to_seconds(lubridate::hms(as.character(.x))))
        }
    )
  )

# Verify that all time split are of <time>
glimpse(time_fomatted_male)
```

Check for any NA values

```{R}
time_fomatted_male %>% filter(if_any(everything(), is.na))
```

We observed 784 rows contain NA values. Since only a small fraction (784 out of 12500 rows) of cases have several missings, we will drop these cases.

Check distinct City.

```{R}
time_fomatted_male %>% group_by(City) %>% summarise(count = n())
```

We observe the oddness that all City are recorded as "N/A" as characters instead of true NA values. Since City is totally missing for all entries and does not carry significance to the analysis, we will drop the City variable.

Check distinct Division.

```{R}
time_fomatted_male %>% group_by(Division) %>% summarise(count = n())
```

We observe that all athletes are HYROX PRO Division (ignore NA since it will be dropped later), which is correct based on our project scope. For easy gender reference, we will add a "MALE" remark – "MALE HYROX PRO".

Based on all inspection made, we will now clean szn8_male_pro and saved into a new male_pro_clean.

```{R}
male_pro_clean <- time_fomatted_male %>%
  # drop all NA cases
  filter(!if_any(everything(), is.na)) %>%
  # deselect City and athlete_url column
  select(- City, - athlete_url) %>%
  # remark MALE in Division
  mutate(
    Division = "MALE HYROX PRO"
  )
  

male_pro_clean %>% head()
```

### Inspect szn8_female_pro

Data cleaning approach is similar as szn8_female_pro.

```{R}
# Standardize all time columns to strict <time> (hms class)
time_fomatted_female <- szn8_female_pro %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      all_of(all_time_cols),
      ~ if (inherits(.x, "hms") || inherits(.x, "difftime")) {
        hms::as_hms(as.numeric(.x))
      } else {
        hms::as_hms(period_to_seconds(lubridate::hms(as.character(.x))))
      }
    )
  )

# Verify that all time split are of <time>
glimpse(time_fomatted_female)
```

Dropping cases and imputing values.

```{R}
female_pro_clean <- time_fomatted_female %>%
  # drop all NA cases
  filter(!if_any(everything(), is.na)) %>%
  # deselect City and athlete_url column
  select(- City, - athlete_url) %>%
  # remark FEMALE in Division
  mutate(
    Division = "FEMALE HYROX PRO"
  )


female_pro_clean %>% head()
```

### Combining male and female into a single dataset

```{R}
combined_pro_clean <- bind_rows(
  male_pro_clean,
  female_pro_clean
)

glimpse(combined_pro_clean)
```

Check if both male and female data exist in combined dataset.

```{R}
combined_pro_clean %>% filter(Division == "MALE HYROX PRO") %>% head()
```

```{R}
combined_pro_clean %>% filter(Division == "FEMALE HYROX PRO") %>% head()
```

Both MALE and FEMALE data exist in the combined dataset.

## Descriptive Analysis

### 1. Running trajectory and slowdown

```{R}
combined_long <- combined_pro_clean %>%
  select(
    Division,
    starts_with("Running_")
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("Running_"),
    names_to = "Run_Name",
    values_to = "Run_Time"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Run_Num = as.numeric(str_extract(Run_Name, "\\d+")),
    Time_Sec = as.numeric(Run_Time)
  )
```

Generate summary of running Q1, Q2 or median, Q3

```{R}
run_summary <- combined_long %>%
  group_by(Division, Run_Num) %>%
  summarise(
    Q1_Sec    = quantile(Time_Sec, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    Median_Sec = median(Time_Sec, na.rm = TRUE),
    Q3_Sec    = quantile(Time_Sec, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    Coef_Variation = sd(Time_Sec) / mean(Time_Sec), 
    .groups = "drop"
  )
  
run_summary %>% arrange(Run_Num)
```

Vizualize median run split time with interquartile range against run station with a line chart.

```{R}
ggplot(run_summary, aes(x = Run_Num, y = Median_Sec, color = Division, fill = Division, group = Division)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q1_Sec, ymax = Q3_Sec), alpha = 0.25, color = NA) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  # Vertical dashed line after Station 4 / Run 4
  geom_vline(xintercept = 4.5, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray40", linewidth = 0.7) +
  # Differentiate colour based on division
  scale_color_manual(values = c("FEMALE HYROX PRO" ="#E377C2", "MALE HYROX PRO" = "#1F77B4")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("FEMALE HYROX PRO" = "#E377C2", "MALE HYROX PRO" = "#1F77B4")) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:8, labels = paste("Run", 1:8)) +
  labs(
    title = "HYROX Run-Time Trajectory",
    subtitle = "Median run split times with Interquartile Range; Dashed line marks Mid Race",
    x = "Run Segment",
    y = "Split Time (seconds)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "top",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, color = "gray30")
  )
```

WHAT DO WE OBSERVE?

### 2. Slowdown summary and early–later association

```{R}
analysis_data <- combined_pro_clean %>%
  mutate(
    Early_Run_Mean = rowMeans(across(all_of(run_cols[1:4]), as.numeric), na.rm = TRUE),
    Later_Run_Mean = rowMeans(across(all_of(run_cols[5:8]), as.numeric), na.rm = TRUE),
    Slowdown_Percentage = 100 * (Later_Run_Mean - Early_Run_Mean) / Early_Run_Mean
  )

analysis_data %>% head()
```

Generate Q1, median and Q3 slowdown percentage summary.

```{R}
slowdown_summary <- analysis_data %>%
  group_by(Division) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(), 
    Q1_Percentage = as.numeric(quantile(Slowdown_Percentage, 0.25)),
    Median_Percentage = median(Slowdown_Percentage),
    Q3_Percentage = as.numeric(quantile(Slowdown_Percentage, 0.75)),
    Percentage_Slower = 100 * mean(Slowdown_Percentage > 0),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

slowdown_summary
```

Spearman rank correlation between early and later run mean, overall and by division. Spearman is used because run times are non-normal and skewed, and extreme outliers are down-weighted.

```{R}
cor(analysis_data$Early_Run_Mean, analysis_data$Later_Run_Mean, method = "spearman")

analysis_data %>%
  group_by(Division) %>%
  summarise(
    Spearman_Rho = cor(Early_Run_Mean, Later_Run_Mean, method = "spearman"),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

We observe females division Spearman corrrelation score (0.7416122) is higher than males (0.6522994), indicating females early run mean has a bigger impact on later run mean compared to males. Both division has relatively positive Spearman score (\> 0.5), therefore late-run performance is largely predictable from early pace.

Scatterplot with per-division linear trend lines.

```{R}
ggplot(analysis_data, 
       aes(
         x = Early_Run_Mean, 
         y = Later_Run_Mean, 
         color = Division)
      ) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.15, size = 0.9) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, linewidth = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~ Division, nrow = 2)
  scale_color_manual(values = c("FEMALE HYROX PRO" = "#E377C2", "MALE HYROX PRO" = "#1F77B4")) +
  labs(
    title = "Later Run Mean versus Early Run Mean",
    subtitle = "Each point is one athlete-race; lines are per-division linear fits",
    x = "Mean Runs 1–4 (seconds)",
    y = "Mean Runs 5–8 (seconds)",
    color = "Division"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "top",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, color = "gray30")
  )
```

## Predictive Analysis

The goal is to predict later-run performance (mean of Runs 5–8) at the mid-race checkpoint using only the first four run splits.

All models are evaluated with 10-fold cross-validation using the same folds, so comparisons are fair.

```{R}
# Set up cross-validation
set.seed(5145)

# Create a row_id field for table-joining later; Division as factor for the random forest
model_data <- analysis_data %>%
  mutate(
    .row_id = row_number(),
    Division = factor(Division)
  )

# Shared 10-fold indices used by the caret models and the baseline
folds <- createFolds(model_data$Later_Run_Mean, k = 10, returnTrain = TRUE)

train_control <- trainControl(
  method = "cv",
  number = 10,
  index = folds,
  savePredictions = "final"
)
```

Two models are compared:

- **Linear model:** later mean on early mean (`Early_Run_Mean * Division` gives each division its own intercept and slope).
- **Random forest:** a nonlinear benchmark testing whether the linear form is too restrictive.

```{R}
lm_cv <- train(
  Later_Run_Mean ~ Early_Run_Mean * Division,
  data = model_data,
  method = "lm",
  trControl = train_control
)

lm_cv
```

```{R}
rf_cv <- train(
  Later_Run_Mean ~ Early_Run_Mean + Division,
  data = model_data,
  method = "rf",
  tuneGrid = data.frame(mtry = 2), # 2 predictors, use both per split
  trControl = train_control
)

rf_cv
```

Compare out-of-fold performance of the three models using RMSE, MAE and R². MAE is less affected by outliers than RMSE because errors are not squared.

```{R}

lm_rf_metrics <- bind_rows(
  lm_cv$results %>% mutate(Model = "Linear model (early mean by division)"),
  rf_cv$results %>% mutate(Model = "Random forest")
) %>%
  select(Model, RMSE, MAE, Rsquared)


lm_rf_metrics
```

We observe te MAE of both linear model (12.40229) and random forest (12.62731) are very similar, however the R2 or linear model (0.7042621) shows a more positive value (0.6934543) compared to random forest.

Build the prediction corridor from out-of-fold residual quantiles of the linear model, then check empirical coverage by division.

```{R}
lm_oof <- lm_cv$pred %>%
  left_join(model_data %>% select(.row_id, Division), by = c("rowIndex" = ".row_id"))

band <- quantile(lm_oof$obs - lm_oof$pred, c(0.05, 0.95))

corridor_coverage <- lm_oof %>%
  mutate(
    Lower = pred + band[1],
    Upper = pred + band[2],
    In_Corridor = obs >= Lower & obs <= Upper
  ) %>%
  group_by(Division) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    Coverage_Pct = 100 * mean(In_Corridor),
    Corridor_Width_Sec = mean(Upper - Lower),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

corridor_coverage
```

To visualise the residual of the linear model fitted on all data, a residual-versus-fitted plot checks constant variance and the QQ plot checks approximate normality, which underlie how the corridor is interpreted.

```{R}
lm_final <- lm(Later_Run_Mean ~ Early_Run_Mean * Division, data = model_data)
summary(lm_final)

diag_data <- tibble(
  Fitted = fitted(lm_final),
  Residual = resid(lm_final)
)

ggplot(diag_data, aes(sample = Residual)) +
  stat_qq(alpha = 0.3, size = 0.8, color = "#1F77B4") +
  stat_qq_line(color = "gray30", linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
    title = "Normal QQ Plot of Residuals",
    x = "Theoretical Quantiles",
    y = "Sample Quantiles"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11)
  )
```
